new: Finite derivatives and Gaussian expectations are distinct from integration along a training trajectory. The finite typed language in @thm-mfp-finite-derivative-program admits smooth polynomial-growth coordinate maps, normalized contractions, causal scalar feedback and exact derivative compilation under fixed Gaussian root laws; its scalar outputs converge in every finite $L^p$. This does not cover unrestricted parameter-tensor contractions, growing program length or derivative order, positive-time reconstruction, or convergence of an infinite training-time Taylor series. The other results retain their own broader root laws, lower regularity or specialized coupling conclusions. [Chapter 7](07-observable-closure.qmd#ch-observable-closure) treats closure and approximation boundaries; [Chapter 8](08-autonomous-computation.qmd#ch-autonomous-computation) supplies quantitative refinement and convergent autonomous computation.

old: For a **fixed** program with subGaussian root marginals, C2 activations with bounded first and second derivatives, and products $b(z)q$ with bounded $C^{1}$ $b,b'$, the values in A.1 also have the ordinary named-source response formulas obtained by truncating each such product. This is a fixed-program specialization, not an all-moment theorem for arbitrary scalar-feedback programs.
new: For a **fixed** program with subGaussian root marginals, C2 activations with bounded first and second derivatives, and products $b(z)q$ with bounded $C^{1}$ $b,b'$, the values in A.1 also have the ordinary named-source response formulas obtained by truncating each such product. This is a fixed-program specialization, not an all-moment theorem for arbitrary scalar-feedback programs. For smooth Gaussian programs in its declared finite language, @thm-mfp-finite-derivative-program separately proves all finite scalar moments and permits causal scalar feedback. Its stronger regularity and Gaussian-root assumptions do not enlarge the present specialization.
